title: Quiz App: How It Works
description: A short quiz about this quiz app — its URL parameters, file format, and behaviour.

questions.text: Where can you put the quiz URL? Select all that apply.
questions.explanation: Use the query string (?quiz=<url>) or the hash (#quiz=<url>, or just #<url>). The hash leaves the query string free for hosts that need it, such as gistpreview's ?<gist-id>. If both are present, the hash wins.

questions.text: What happens when the page is opened without a quiz parameter?
options: It shows a home page with help and an input box for the quiz URL
questions.explanation: The home page explains the format and lets you paste a URL; submitting reloads the page with #quiz=<url>.

questions.text: Which of these quiz URLs can be loaded? Select all that apply.
options: A file on a server that does not send CORS headers
questions.explanation: Relative paths are resolved against the page. Cross-origin files load only when the server allows CORS — GitHub raw and gist raw do; a server without CORS headers is blocked by the browser.

questions.text: In a question object, what does "correct": 2 mean?
questions.explanation: Indexes are zero-based: 0 is the first option, so 2 is the third.

questions.text: How do you make a question multiple-choice?
questions.explanation: When correct is an array, the options become checkboxes and a Submit button appears. You must choose exactly the right set to score.

questions.text: Which fields of a question are required? Select all that apply.
questions.explanation: section and explanation are optional. At the top level, title and description are optional too, and you may even supply a bare array of questions.

questions.text: A quiz file contains <img src=x onerror=alert(1)> in an explanation. What happens?
options: The tag is dropped because only an allow-list of tags is kept, without attributes
questions.explanation: Content is parsed in an inert document and rebuilt from an allow-list (e.g. strong, em, code, pre, ul, a…). Unknown tags are unwrapped, dangerous ones like script are removed, and all attributes except a safe link href are stripped.

questions.text: Which of these are kept when rendering quiz text? Select all that apply.
questions.explanation: Formatting tags and safe links survive. Scripts are removed entirely, and inline styles (like every other attribute) are stripped.

questions.text: You answer half the questions and reload the page. What happens?
options: Your answers are restored from your browser's local storage
Answers are fetched from a server
questions.explanation: Progress is saved in localStorage per quiz URL. If the quiz file changes, the saved progress is discarded. Use Restart quiz on the results page to start over.

questions.text: What does adding &shuffle=1 after the quiz URL in the hash do?
options: Picks a random subset of questions
questions.explanation: Both the question order and each question's option order are shuffled. The order is saved with your progress, so reloading doesn't reshuffle mid-quiz.

questions.text: Which keyboard shortcuts are supported while answering? Select all that apply.
options: Letters <kbd>A</kbd>–<kbd>Z</kbd> or digits <kbd>1</kbd>–<kbd>9</kbd> to pick an option
<kbd>Enter</kbd> to submit or go to the next question
questions.explanation: Answers are locked once given — there's no undo, but you can restart the quiz from the results page.

questions.text: How is the initial colour theme chosen?
options: From your last choice, falling back to your OS colour-scheme preference
From a field in the quiz file
questions.explanation: The toggle in the top-right switches between dark and light; your choice is remembered. Before you choose, the app follows prefers-color-scheme.
